comments.text: Level data $7EC0-$7EC1: Loaded level identifier (3), checked at $16A6, then the first entry of the five-byte table that $09AB reads with the level number as index for multicolour 1 ($D022). That first entry is Klondike's, 8 in every level's load, so nothing reads it while this level plays; this level's entry is $7EC4 in the resident part.

Level data $8192-$8391: The rest of the actor-template directory: two-byte pointers, the low-index half to $827B and the high-index half from $827C, read by $4EF9 and by the creators that double a template number and read $827C,Y. The highest template a creator names is $F0, whose pointer is at $835C-$835D. From $835E: the variables $835E and $835F, tables at $8360-$836E read by $4C50-$4C7A and $2315, then the random-spawn tables that $3D2B reads by level: masks at $836F, record bases at $8374 (low) and $8379 (high), and from $837E the four-byte random-spawn records described at $8392.

Level data $8392-$83DF: Four-byte random-spawn records, the same in every level, continuing from $837E. $3D2B picks one with the level's mask at $836F and base at $8374/$8379 and spawns it through $3B4B when its position, bytes 0 and 1 (low, high), is less than $28 ahead of the scroll position $516D/$516E; bytes 2 and 3 are the row and the template. A record of FF FF 00 00 spawns nothing.
Level data $8F00-$8FBF: Level-specific continuation of the actor shape stream read at $8EC0 plus a byte index. $FF introduces a loop index, or $FF/$FF ends the actor.

Level data $8FC0-$90DF: Five parallel exit tables of 30 entries each: edge selector bytes at $8FC0 (0 for the top edge, 1 for the bottom), source world block words at $8FDE, destination scroll position words at $901A, right scroll limit words at $9056 and destination X block bytes at $9092. The exit handler at $3096 searches the first 22 entries, the count for this level in $806C. Only 21 are filled: the 22nd is all zeros, a top-edge exit at world block 0, and so are the eight after it. $90B0-$90DF are 48 zero bytes after the tables that nothing reads.

Level data $90E0-$9141: Two path pointer directories of 18 two-byte pointers each, $FFFF for none, used by $418E: $90E0-$9103 point to the magnitude streams and $9104-$9127 to the direction streams (10 of each in use in this level). $9128-$9141 is the 26-byte actor template $37, which the directory entry at $81EA points to and $4730 creates.

Level data $9142-$9341: Actor initialisation records addressed through the template directory. The two constructor readers copy 26 bytes into display, collision, health, animation and motion arrays; offset 6 is score class in $3C32 and X expansion in $4F04.

Level data $9342-$9541: Actor initialisation records addressed through the template directory. The two constructor readers copy 26 bytes into display, collision, health, animation and motion arrays; offset 6 is score class in $3C32 and X expansion in $4F04.

Level data $9542-$9741: The last actor templates, then path streams. $9542-$9551 is the last 16 bytes of the template at $9538, and $9552-$9689 holds 12 more, 26 bytes apart from $9552 to $9670 (template numbers $B0-$BB in the directory at $817C): the last of the 53 templates that run from $9128. The two constructor readers copy 26 bytes into display, collision, health, animation and motion arrays; offset 6 is score class in $3C32 and X expansion in $4F04. From $968A the bytes are path streams, which $418E reads through the pointer directories at $90E0 (magnitudes, each stream ending in a command byte from $FC to $FF) and $9104 (directions, one byte for each magnitude). The streams that start here, each path's magnitudes then its directions: path 0 at $968A and $96B0, 1 at $96D9 and $96EE, 2 at $9702 and $9710 and 3 at $971E, with its directions at $975E. The magnitude stream of path 3 runs on past $9741, to $975D. The directory entries for template numbers $C6-$F0 all hold $968A, the address after the last template, so they lead to path stream 0 and not to a template; no spawn record of this level names any of them.

Level data $9742-$9941: Not actor templates: this level's 26-byte templates end at $9689. They are path streams, which $418E reads through the pointer directories at $90E0 (magnitudes, each stream ending in a command byte from $FC to $FF) and $9104 (directions, one byte for each magnitude). The piece opens inside the magnitude stream of path 3, which starts at $971E. The streams that start here, each path's magnitudes then its directions: path 3 at $975E for its directions (its magnitudes start at $971E), 4 at $979D and $97C0, 5 at $97E2 and $9822, 6 at $9862 and $9887, 7 at $98AB and $98C6, 8 at $98E0 and $9903 and 9 at $9925, with its directions at $9956. The magnitude stream of path 9 runs on past $9941, to $9955.

Level data $9942-$9AFF: Not actor templates: this level's 26-byte templates end at $9689. To $9985 they are path streams, which $418E reads through the pointer directories at $90E0 (magnitudes, each stream ending in a command byte from $FC to $FF) and $9104 (directions, one byte for each magnitude). The piece opens inside the magnitude stream of path 9, which starts at $9925. One stream starts here, that of path 9 at $9956 for its directions (its magnitudes start at $9925). The last stream byte is at $9985. $9986-$9AFF: 378 bytes that no pointer in either path directory leads to and no instruction names. They are the same bytes as the Klondike load has at these addresses, where they are part of its path streams.
Level data $A000-$A1FF: Four-byte actor spawn records, read by $3B4B: world position high byte, position low byte, row, template identifier. Special template identifiers activate a guardian.

Level data $A200-$A3FF: Four-byte actor spawn records continuing from $A000, read by $3B4B: world position high byte, position low byte, row, template identifier. Special template identifiers activate a guardian. The list ends with the record 7F FF 00 00 at $A388; the bytes from $A38C to $A3FF are zeros that nothing reads.

Level data $A400-$A40F: Zero bytes after the end of the spawn list. The list ends with the record 7F FF 00 00 at $A388, a position the scroll never reaches, so the record cursor stops there and nothing reads the zeros from $A38C.

Level data $A410-$A60F: Six-block-high map stream. Each byte selects a 4-by-4-character definition at $B000 plus 16 times the block number; the map reader advances six bytes per block column. Area exits can replace its read pointer.
